question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}6\left(\frac{x}{4y+1}\right)\text{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j\,$ for $0\le t\le 6?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j,$ then along the curve we have $x=t$ and $y={t}^{2}.$ 

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =i+2tj \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, if  $f(x,y)=6\left(\frac{x}{4y+1}\right)$, then we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =6\left(\frac{t}{4{t}^{2}+1}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}6\left(\frac{x}{4y+1}\right)\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{6}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t  \\    & =6\left({\int }_{0}^{6}(\frac{t}{4{t}^{2}+1})\cdot \sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \text{d}t\right) \\    & =6\left({\int }_{0}^{6}\frac{t}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}}\text{d}t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s,$ where $f(x,y)=6\left(\sqrt{2}(x-y)\right)$ and the curve $C$ is parametrized 
 by $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}+t,\,{t}^{2}-t⟩$ for $t\in [0,6]?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}+t,\,{t}^{2}-t⟩,$ then along the curve we have $x={t}^{2}+t,$ and $y={t}^{2}-t.$ 

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t)j \\  & =(2t+1)\,i+(2t-1)\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2t+1)^{2}+(2t-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+4t+1+4{t}^{2}-4t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{8{t}^{2}+2} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since $f(x,y)=6\left(\sqrt{2}(x-y)\right)$, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =6\left(\sqrt{2}[({t}^{2}+t)-({t}^{2}-t)]\right) \\    & =6\left(2\sqrt{2}t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{6}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t  \\    & =6\left({\int }_{0}^{6}2\sqrt{2}t\cdot \sqrt{2}\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \text{d}t\right) \\    & =6\left(4{\int }_{0}^{6}t\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}s,$ where $f(x,y,z)=6\left(2x-{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}\right)$ and the curve $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,t-1,\,t+1⟩$ for $t\in [0,6]?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,t-1,\,t+1⟩,$ then along the curve we have $x={t}^{2},$ $y=t-1,$ and $z=t+1.$ 

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)k \\  & =2t\,i+j+k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+2}\end{aligned}
$$

  

Now, since $f(x,y,z)=6\left(2x-{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}\right)$, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =6\left(2({t}^{2})-(t-1)^{2}-(t+1)^{2}\right) \\    & =6\left(2{t}^{2}-({t}^{2}-2t+1)-({t}^{2}+2t+1)\right) \\    & =6\left(2{t}^{2}-{t}^{2}+2t-1-{t}^{2}-2t-1\right) \\    & =6\left(-2\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{6}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t  \\    & =6\left({\int }_{0}^{6}(-2)\cdot \sqrt{4{t}^{2}+2}\cdot \text{d}t\right) \\    & =6\left({\int }_{0}^{6}(-2)\cdot \sqrt{2(2{t}^{2}+1)}\cdot \text{d}t\right) \\    & =6\left({\int }_{0}^{6}(-2)\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2{t}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}t\right) \\    & =6\left(-2\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{6}\sqrt{2{t}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}s,$ where $f(x,y,z)=6\left(x+y-z\right)$ and the curve $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}+1,\,{t}^{2}-1,\,{t}^{2}⟩$ for $t\in [0,6]?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}+1,\,{t}^{2}-1,\,{t}^{2}⟩,$ then along the curve we have $x={t}^{2}+1,$ $y={t}^{2}-1,$ and $z={t}^{2}.$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+1)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-1)j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})k \\  & =2t\,i+2t\,j+2t\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+4{t}^{2}+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12{t}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}|t| \\  & =2\sqrt{3}t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $|t|=t$ since $t\ge 0$ along the path of $C.$

Now, since $f(x,y,z)=6\left(x+y-z\right)$, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =6\left(({t}^{2}+1)+({t}^{2}-1)-{t}^{2}\right) \\    & =6\left(2{t}^{2}-{t}^{2}\right) \\    & =6\left({t}^{2}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{6}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t  \\    & =6\left({\int }_{0}^{6}{t}^{2}\cdot 2\sqrt{3}t\cdot \text{d}t\right) \\    & =6\left(2\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{6}{t}^{3}\,\text{d}t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}6\left(z({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\right)\,\text{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j\,+t\,k$ for $\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi}{12}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j\,+t\,k,$ then along the curve we have $x=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$ $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,$ and $z=t.$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)k \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

  

Now, if $f(x,y,z)=6\left(z({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\right)$, then we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =6\left(t((\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}-(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2})\right) \\    & =6\left(t({cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t)\right) \\    & =6\left(t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as  

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}6\left(z({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\right)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t  \\    & =6\left({\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \text{d}t\right) \\    & =6\left(\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{12}}t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,\text{d}t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =-6\left(t((\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}-(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2})\right) \\    & =-6\left(t({cos}^{2}⁡t-{sin}^{2}⁡t)\right) \\    & =-6\left(t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as  

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-6\left(z({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\right)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{\frac{5 \pi}{12}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t  \\    & =-6\left({\int }_{\frac{5 \pi}{12}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot \text{d}t\right) \\    & =-6\left(\sqrt{2}{\int }_{\frac{5 \pi}{12}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,\text{d}t\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to the integral $\displaystyle \int_C6\left((x^{3} - y)\right)ds$, where the curve $C$ is parametrized by $r(t) = 2ti + (2 - t)j$ for $-2\le t\le 1$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=\langle 2 t, 2 - t\rangle,$ then along the curve we have $x=2 t$, $y=2 - t$.

Computing $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j \\ &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 t)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 - t)j \\ &= (2)\,i+(-1)\,j \\ \|r'(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2} \\ &= \sqrt{(2)^2+(-1)^2} \\ &= \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=6 x^{3} - 6 y$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=6\left((2 t)^3-(2 - t)\right) \\ &= 6\left(8t^3-2+t\right) \\ &= 48 t^{3} + 6 t - 12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{-2}^{1} f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= \int_{-2}^{1}(48 t^{3} + 6 t - 12)(\sqrt{5})\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= \int_{-2}^{1}6 \sqrt{5} \left(8 t^{3} + t - 2\right)\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=-6\left((2 t)^3-(2 - t)\right) \\ &= -6\left(8t^3-2+t\right) \\ &= - 48 t^{3} - 6 t + 12.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\int_C x y - z^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=\langle t^{2}, t + 1, t + 1\rangle$ for $0\le t\le \frac{3}{2}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=\langle t^{2}, t + 1, t + 1\rangle,$ then along the curve we have $x=t^{2}$, $y=t + 1$, $z=t + 1$.

Computing $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j+\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}t}\,k \\ &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t^{2})i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t + 1)j+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t + 1)k \\ &= (2 t)\,i+(1)\,j+(1)\,k \\ \|r'(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}t})^2} \\ &= \sqrt{(2 t)^2+(1)^2+(1)^2} \\ &= \sqrt{4 t^{2} + 2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y,z)=x y - z^{2}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=(t^{2})(t + 1)-(t + 1)^2 \\ &= 1t^3+(1)t^2-\left(1t^2+(2)t+1\right) \\ &= t^{3} - 2 t - 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{0}^{\frac{3}{2}} f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= \int_{0}^{\frac{3}{2}}(t^{3} - 2 t - 1)(\sqrt{4 t^{2} + 2})\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= \int_{0}^{\frac{3}{2}}\sqrt{4 t^{2} + 2} \left(t^{3} - 2 t - 1\right)\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to $\int_C - 3 x y + 3 z^{2}\,\mathrm{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=\langle 3 t^{2}, 3 t - 3, 3 t + 3\rangle$ for $1\le t\le 3$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=\langle 3 t^{2}, 3 t - 3, 3 t + 3\rangle,$ then along the curve we have $x=3 t^{2}$, $y=3 t - 3$, $z=3 t + 3$.

Computing $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j+\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}t}\,k \\ &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 t^{2})i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 t - 3)j+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 t + 3)k \\ &= (6 t)\,i+(3)\,j+(3)\,k \\ \|r'(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}t})^2} \\ &= \sqrt{(6 t)^2+(3)^2+(3)^2} \\ &= \sqrt{36 t^{2} + 18}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y,z)=- 3 x y + 3 z^{2}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=-3\left((3 t^{2})(3 t - 3)-(3 t + 3)^2\right) \\ &= -3\left(9t^3+(-9)t^2-\left(9t^2+(18)t+9\right)\right) \\ &= - 27 t^{3} + 54 t^{2} + 54 t + 27.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C f(x,y,z)\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{1}^{3} f(r(t))\,\|r'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= \int_{1}^{3}(- 27 t^{3} + 54 t^{2} + 54 t + 27)(\sqrt{36 t^{2} + 18})\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &= \int_{1}^{3}\sqrt{4 t^{2} + 2} \left(- 81 t^{3} + 162 t^{2} + 162 t + 81\right)\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
